+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'Resource paths: accept an absolute path that is in a layer directory of the skill'
+---
+## What
+The model sometimes gives an absolute path, for example after `read resource` gives the absolute path of a binary file. `read resource` and `run script` must accept it, but only when the path is in a layer directory of the skill. The model can give a path relative to the skill, and that path must work as it does now.
+
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/SkillOverlay.swift`: add `internal func relativePath(for path: String) -> String?`.
+  - A relative path comes back with no change.
+  - An absolute path: make it standard and resolve symlinks (for example `/tmp` and `/private/tmp`). Then compare it with each URL of `directories`, with the same standardization. If the path is in a directory, return the part after that directory, for example `references/changelog.md`. If the path is in no directory, return `nil`.
+  - A path that is the directory itself, or a path that gives an empty relative part, returns `nil`.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/ReadResource.swift`: in `execute(in:)`, call `overlay.relativePath(for: path)` first. Use the relative path for `resolve`, `size` and `scan`, and use it as the `path` of `ReadResourceResult`. If the result is `nil`, give `ResourcePathRules.deniedMessage(path:)` with the path that the model gave.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/RunScript.swift`: apply the same rule before the `scripts/` check and the gates. The model gets one rule for all resource operations.
+- After the relative path is found, the overlay always reads the winning copy. Thus an absolute path into a lower layer reads the copy of the highest layer that holds that relative path.
+- `ResourcePathRules.isWellFormedRelativePath(_:)` does not change. It checks the relative path after the conversion.
+- Update the `path` parameter description in `ReadResource.parameterMetadata` and `RunScript.parameterMetadata`: "The path of the file, relative to the skill directory, for example `references/guide.md`. An absolute path in the skill directory also works."
+- `docs/operations.md`: in the operations table, say that `read resource` and `run script` accept an absolute path in a layer directory of the skill, and that each other absolute path is refused.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `read resource` with `path: "references/changelog.md"` gives the same result as now.
+- [ ] `read resource` with the absolute path of that file in a layer directory of the skill gives the same content, and the result `path` is `references/changelog.md`.
+- [ ] An absolute path into a lower layer gives the winning copy of the highest layer.
+- [ ] An absolute path outside each layer directory of the skill (for example `/etc/hosts`, or a file of a different skill) gives the denied corrective message.
+- [ ] An absolute path with `..` that goes out of the skill directory gives the denied corrective message.
+- [ ] `run script` accepts an absolute path to a file in `scripts/` of the skill, and refuses an absolute path outside the skill.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/SkillOverlayTests.swift`: unit tests of `relativePath(for:)`: relative, absolute inside, absolute in a lower layer, absolute outside, the directory itself, a `/private/tmp` symlink form, and `..` escape.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/ReadResourceTests.swift`: a relative read and an absolute read of the same file give equal content; an absolute path outside the skill gives the denied message.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/RunScriptTests.swift`: an absolute script path in the skill runs; an absolute path outside the skill is denied.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes with no failure.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #skill-resources
\ No newline at end of file
